name: Sackcloth
overview: Sackcloth in Scripture is a tangible expression of deep mourning, repentance, and affliction, as seen when Jacob put sackcloth on his loins to mourn Joseph (Genesis 37:34) and when King David and his people girded themselves with sackcloth to mourn Abner (2 Samuel 3:31). It is described as a coarse, rough garment often worn next to the skin, sometimes with ropes on the head, symbolizing humility and sorrow (1 Kings 20:31-32). The use of sackcloth extends to times of national grief and personal affliction, as Rizpah spread sackcloth over the dead to protect them, demonstrating steadfast mourning and care (2 Samuel 21:10). Even kings like Ahab wore sackcloth to express repentance and fasting, showing its role in sincere sorrow before God (1 Kings 21:27).
